issues.legal_issue: A civil suit seeking to invalidate a debt-recovery tribunal decree is barred where the statutory appeal remedy is available and has not been exhausted.
material_facts: The suits sought declarations that a debt-recovery tribunal decree was void and not binding on the property, together with injunctions against recovery action.
The governing debt-recovery scheme provided an appeal against the tribunal’s decree to an appellate tribunal.
The plaintiffs filed civil suits rather than exhausting that appeal remedy.
issues.conclusion: The suits challenging the tribunal decree were not maintainable, and the plaints were liable to be rejected.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 18, 19 and 20 of the Recovery of Debts Due to Banks and Financial Institutions Act, 1993 establish the special recovery framework and an appellate remedy; a civil suit cannot be used to derail that framework where the statutory appeal has not been pursued. Following Punjab National Bank v. O.C. Krishnan, (2001) 6 SCC 569, the availability of the statutory appeal bars recourse to a civil suit challenging the tribunal’s decision.

predicates.civil_suit_challenging_recovery_tribunal: The plaintiff brought a civil suit seeking to invalidate or avoid a decree made in a debt-recovery tribunal proceeding.
predicates.statutory_appeal_available: The governing recovery framework provided an appeal to a specialist appellate body against the tribunal’s decree.
predicates.statutory_appeal_exhausted: The plaintiff pursued and exhausted the available statutory appeal remedy.

issues.definition: When a civil suit challenges a recovery tribunal decree, an available but unexhausted statutory appeal remedy results in the suit being barred and the plaint being rejected.

issues.legal_issue: Fraud allegations that do not materially address the security underlying a recovery decree and are unsupported by specific factual particulars do not prevent rejection of a vexatious plaint.
material_facts: The plaintiffs alleged that fraud had been used to create the security and obtain the recovery decree, but the pleaded fraud concerned a partnership deed rather than the guarantor’s guarantee or mortgage.
The criminal proceedings and conviction relied upon concerned the partnership deed; they did not address the guarantee or mortgage, and the bank was not a party to those proceedings.

The plaintiffs claimed through sale deeds executed by the guarantor as an attorney for the original owners, although the property had already been mortgaged; the guarantor did not disclose the alleged sales when later seeking relief from the tribunal decree.
On a meaningful reading of the plaints, the court found the fraud allegations illusory and the suits vexatious and an abuse of process.
issues.conclusion: The fraud allegations did not save the suits from rejection; the plaints were vexatious and liable to be rejected.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the plaint must be read as a whole and meaningfully, and a plaint may be rejected where it discloses no genuine right to sue or is manifestly vexatious. Fraud must be pleaded with specific material particulars; merely using the word “fraud” does not suffice. The Court applied T. Arivandandam v. T.V. Satyapal, (1977) 4 SCC 467; Church of Christ Charitable Trust v. Ponniamman Educational Trust, (2012) 8 SCC 706; A.B.C. Laminart Pvt. Ltd. v. A.P. Agencies, (1989) 2 SCC 163; Sopan Sukhdeo Sable v. Assistant Charity Commissioner, (2004) 3 SCC 137; Madanuri Sri Rama Chandra Murthy v. Syed Jalal, (2017) 13 SCC 174; and the Madras High Court decision in M/s Cambridge Solutions Ltd. v. Global Software Ltd., 2016-5-L.W. 45.

predicates.civil_suit_seeking_to_avoid_recovery_dec: The plaintiff brought a civil suit seeking to defeat or avoid a decree made in a recovery proceeding.
predicates.fraud_allegations_unconnected_to_securit: The pleaded fraud concerned matters other than the creation or execution of the security relied upon for the recovery decree.
predicates.specific_material_particulars_supporting: The plaintiff pleaded concrete factual particulars and supporting material connecting the alleged fraud to the challenged security or decree.

issues.definition: A suit seeking to avoid a recovery decree is rejected when its fraud allegations do not concern the security underlying the decree and lack specific material particulars.

issues.legal_issue: Vague assertions about when and how a plaintiff discovered a decree or encumbrance do not avoid the limitation bar on a suit brought outside the applicable limitation period.
material_facts: The plaintiffs brought their suits years after the property had been mortgaged and the recovery decree had been made.
The plaints asserted that the plaintiffs had learned of the mortgage and decree only recently, but did not specify when or how they learned of them.
The court found the discovery assertions vague and made only to bring the suits within limitation.
issues.conclusion: The vague discovery assertions did not avoid limitation, and the plaints were liable to be rejected on that ground as well.
issues.legal_principle: For purposes of Order 7 Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure, the plaint must be read as a whole to determine whether the suit is barred by law. A plaintiff relying on delayed discovery to overcome limitation must plead specific facts explaining when and how the relevant matter was discovered; vague assertions are insufficient. The Court also relied on Ram Singh v. Gram Panchayat Mehal Kalan, (1986) 4 SCC 364, for the principle that clever drafting cannot circumvent a legal bar.

predicates.civil_suit_filed_outside_limitation_peri: The plaintiff brought the civil suit after the time allowed for the claim had expired, assessed from the pleaded facts.
predicates.delayed_discovery_relied_on: The plaintiff relied on having discovered the decree, encumbrance, or relevant facts only after they occurred.
predicates.specific_pleading_of_when_and_how_discov: The plaintiff pleaded concrete facts identifying when and how the relevant matter was discovered.

issues.definition: When a suit is brought outside the applicable limitation period and delayed discovery is asserted without specific facts about when and how discovery occurred, the limitation bar applies and the plaint is rejected.
